Description: The Biochemistry, Molecular and Structural Biology (BMSB) Graduate Program is designed for students who want to conduct research at the interface of chemistry, biology and medicine. We are a small, tight-knit program within a large, vibrant research university. Our primary goal is to train the next generation of scientists to be leaders in academia, biotechnology and the pharmaceutical industry. The core of the program is the research experience, where students work in the laboratories of world-renowned faculty to make original and impactful discoveries. Students choose a research advisor from among over 40 faculty members in the Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry. These faculty members have research interests that span the entire range of biochemistry and molecular biology, including structural biology, proteomics, genomics, epigenetics, metabolism, and bioenergetics. The research is often interdisciplinary, involving collaborations with other departments such as microbiology, immunology and molecular genetics; biological chemistry; medicine; and physics. Our faculty are also members of many interdisciplinary research centers and institutes at UCLA, including the Molecular Biology Institute (MBI), the California NanoSystems Institute (CNSI), the Jonsson Comprehensive Cancer Center, and the Eli and Edythe Broad Center of Regenerative Medicine and Stem Cell Research.

ProgramName: Master of Public Health in Environmental Health Sciences
Requirements: Applicants must hold a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited institution with a minimum cumulative grade point average of 3.0. Prerequisite coursework includes one year of general biology, one year of general chemistry, at least one quarter of organic chemistry, and one year of mathematics including at least one quarter of calculus. Application materials include the SOPHAS application, the UCLA Graduate Division supplemental application, three letters of recommendation, a statement of purpose, a personal statement, and a resume/CV.

Description: The Master of Public Health (MPH) degree in Environmental Health Sciences is a professional degree that provides students with the skills and knowledge to address complex environmental health issues. The program prepares students for leadership roles in public health practice, policy, and research. The MPH in Environmental Health Sciences is a two-year program (including a summer internship) that prepares students for careers in the environmental health sciences. The curriculum provides students with a strong foundation in the basic sciences and public health, while allowing for specialization in areas such as toxicology, exposure science, and environmental policy. Students in the program complete a minimum of 56 units of coursework, including a core curriculum in public health and environmental health sciences, and a summer internship in a professional environmental health setting. The program culminates in a comprehensive exam or a capstone project.

Students in the ESE program earn a professional doctorate (Doctor of Environmental Science and Engineering, or D.Env.) rather than a research doctorate (PhD). The ESE Program’s multidisciplinary curriculum and training distinguish it from traditional PhD programs. Students are required to take courses in several different departments and to complete an off-campus internship (the ‘residency’) in an environment-related organization.

The program is designed for students who intend to pursue careers in public health practice, including in government agencies, non-profit organizations, and the private sector. Applicants must submit a UCLA Graduate Division online application, which includes a statement of purpose, personal statement, letters of recommendation, transcripts, and a resume/CV. In addition, applicants must submit program-specific materials including a scholarly writing sample. The GRE is not required for the Ethnomusicology graduate programs.

Description: The Master of Arts in Ethnomusicology provides a broad foundation in the study of ethnomusicology and systematic musicology, as well as related disciplines. It is designed to prepare students for the Ph.D. program. Students are expected to develop a general knowledge of the history, theory, and methodology of ethnomusicology or systematic musicology, and to gain experience in ethnographic fieldwork and musical performance (for those in the ethnomusicology concentration) or in scientific and philosophical methods (for those in the systematic musicology concentration).

Requirements: Applicants are considered for admission for the Fall quarter only. A master's degree in ethnomusicology or a related field is usually required for admission to the Ph.D. program. In some instances, students with only a bachelor's degree may be admitted to the Ph.D. program. Required application materials include a Statement of Purpose, a Personal Statement, a CV or Resume, three letters of recommendation, and one or two examples of written work (preferably on a musical topic).
Department: UCLA Herb Alpert School of Music
Concentration: Ethnomusicology; Systematic Musicology
Description: The Department of Ethnomusicology offers the Master of Arts (M.A.) and Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degrees in Ethnomusicology. The graduate program in Ethnomusicology is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the history, theory, and practice of the field. Students learn to conduct original research on musical traditions from around the world, using a variety of methods including ethnographic fieldwork, archival research, and musical analysis. The program is one of the oldest and largest in the world, with a faculty that includes leading scholars in the field and a student body drawn from across the globe. The Ph.D. in ethnomusicology provides students with the tools to conduct original research on music as a cultural and social phenomenon. Students work closely with faculty members to develop their research projects, which often involve extensive fieldwork and archival research. The program emphasizes both theoretical rigor and practical skills, preparing students for careers in academia, public sector work, and the arts. Students in the Ph.D. program in Ethnomusicology are expected to develop a high level of expertise in at least one musical tradition and to gain a broad understanding of the field as a whole. The program also offers students the opportunity to participate in performance ensembles, which provide hands-on experience in a variety of musical traditions. Graduate students in Ethnomusicology may also elect to complete a specialization in Systematic Musicology.

Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited institution with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0. Additionally, applicants must demonstrate advocacy or counseling experience (volunteer or paid) and exposure to the genetic counseling profession. Required materials include three letters of recommendation, a Statement of Purpose, a Personal Statement, and a CV or Resume.

The program is housed in the Department of Human Genetics at the David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA. The mission of the UCLA Master of Science in Genetic Counseling program is to provide students with a comprehensive foundation in the science of genetics, the counseling skills needed to assist patients in understanding and adapting to the medical, psychological, and familial implications of genetic contributions to disease, and the research skills to advance the field. Students benefit from an extensive and diverse clinical training environment available at UCLA and its affiliated medical centers.

Description: The UCLA School of Nursing offers a Master of Science in Nursing (MSN) degree to two groups of students: those with a natural science or social science degree in another field who want to become a registered nurse (MECN) and those who have a BSN degree and want to become an advanced practice nurse (APRN). The APRN program is designed for registered nurses with a Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) who wish to prepare for roles as Nurse Practitioners or Clinical Nurse Specialists in specific populations.

The PhD program offers a curriculum that builds on previous knowledge and experience, provides a foundation in nursing science and research methodology, and allows for the pursuit of individual research interests.

The BSN to DNP pathway provides students with the clinical expertise and leadership skills needed to improve health outcomes and provide high-level care for individuals and populations. The curriculum focuses on clinical practice, leadership, health policy, and evidence-based practice.

Students take courses in the basic sciences as well as in oral biology. Areas of study include, but are not limited to, immunology, microbiology, developmental biology, cell biology, molecular biology, and neuroscience.

Description: The Department of Philosophy offers the Master of Arts (M.A.) and Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degrees in Philosophy. The department does not admit students whose goal is only the M.A. degree. The Ph.D. program is designed to develop the student’s ability to do original and creative research in philosophy. The program is structured to give students a broad knowledge of the history of philosophy and of its various fields, as well as an intensive knowledge of the area of their specialization. Students are encouraged to pursue their studies in a way that relates philosophy to other disciplines.

Description: The department offers the Master of Science (M.S.) and Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degrees in Physics. The graduate program in physics at UCLA is designed to provide students with a broad and deep understanding of the fundamental principles of physics and their application to a variety of physical systems. It is also intended to develop their ability to conduct original research. The department offers a wide range of research opportunities in Atomic, Molecular, and Optical Physics; Biophysics; Condensed Matter Physics; Elementary Particle Physics; Plasma Physics; and Nuclear Physics.

Description: The Department of Physics and Astronomy offers the Master of Science (M.S.) and Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degrees in Physics. The primary goal of the graduate program in Physics is to train students for careers in research and teaching at the university level, or for research and development positions in government or industry.

If a doctoral or master’s degree is not from an accredited US institution, the applicant must have at least five years of professional experience in a health-related field following the completion of the bachelor’s degree. Students gain a broad understanding of the public health sciences, including epidemiology, biostatistics, environmental health, health policy and management, and social and behavioral sciences. The curriculum is designed to be completed in two years of part-time study, allowing students to continue their professional work while pursuing their degree. The program is offered in a hybrid format, with a combination of in-person and online instruction.

The DrPH program focuses on providing students with the advanced knowledge and skills needed to address complex public health challenges, lead multidisciplinary teams, and translate research into practice.

Description: The UCLA Master of Quantitative Economics (MQE) is a STEM-certified program designed for students who want to become experts at analyzing data and solving complex problems in the global economy. In today’s data-driven world, economists need to be able to use data to tell a story and provide insights that lead to better decision-making. The MQE program provides students with the tools they need to succeed in a variety of careers, including finance, consulting, and data science. Our world-renowned faculty teach students how to apply economic theory to real-world problems. We also offer a variety of professional development opportunities, including internships and career coaching. If you are looking for a program that will challenge you and prepare you for a successful career in economics, the UCLA MQE program is the right choice for you.

This can be demonstrated by a bachelor’s degree in a Scandinavian language or the equivalent. The program provides students with the opportunity to study the languages, literatures, and cultures of the Scandinavian countries in a broad European and global context. Students may focus their studies on any of the Scandinavian languages (Danish, Icelandic, Norwegian, Old Norse, or Swedish) and their respective literatures and cultures from the Middle Ages to the present.

The program offers students the opportunity to specialize in either a particular national literature or in Old Norse/Icelandic and medieval studies. The Ph.D. program is designed to prepare students for research and teaching at the university level. The program consists of two primary areas: Scandinavian Literature and Old Norse Studies, and is characterized by its interdisciplinarity and its strengths in film and media, environmental humanities, and gender and sexuality studies.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Slavic, East European and Eurasian Languages and Cultures

Description: Our graduate program is designed to provide students with a comprehensive and rigorous training in Slavic, East European, and Eurasian languages, literatures, and cultures. We offer both M.A. and Ph.D. degrees, with tracks in Literature and Linguistics. Our curriculum is tailored to the individual interests and goals of our students, while ensuring a broad and deep understanding of the field. Students work closely with our world-class faculty, who are leading scholars in their respective areas of expertise.

The program is designed to prepare students for careers in research and teaching at the university level, as well as for other professional paths that require high-level expertise in the region.

Application requirements include a Statement of Purpose, a Personal Statement, a current Resume, and three letters of recommendation. Description: The Master of Social Welfare (MSW) program at UCLA Luskin prepares students for leadership in the profession of social work. The program is designed to train students to work with individuals, families, groups, organizations, and communities, providing a solid foundation in social work values, ethics, and practices. Field education serves as the “signature pedagogy” of the program, offering an intensive, supervised learning experience where students transition from the classroom to becoming practitioners in the community. During their field placements, students apply the theories and skills they learn in the classroom to real-world settings under the guidance of experienced social work professionals.

Exceptional students with only a baccalaureate degree may also be considered. A grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) for the last two years of undergraduate study and for any post-baccalaureate study is required. Required application materials include a Statement of Purpose, Personal Statement, CV or Resume, three letters of recommendation, and a Professional Writing Sample. The GRE is not required for admission to this program.
Department: UCLA Luskin School of Public Affairs
Description: Social welfare at UCLA Luskin is a diverse and multidisciplinary field that examines how we can meet the needs of all members of society, particularly those who are marginalized or vulnerable. Our curriculum covers diverse research areas, including health and behavioral health, aging, children and families, globalization and social justice, mental health, and more. Through a combination of rigorous coursework, independent research, and mentorship from world-renowned faculty, students will develop the skills and expertise needed to become leaders in the field and to create positive social change. If you’re ready to take the next step in your academic journey and make a real-world impact, we invite you to explore the PhD in Social Welfare at UCLA Luskin.

Transfer Students: Transfer applicants to the Classical Civilization major with 90 or more units must complete as many of the following courses as possible prior to admission: two courses from classical civilization, ancient Greek or Latin, or ancient history. Refer to the UCLA transfer admission guide for up-to-date information regarding transfer selection for admission.
Description: The Classical Civilization major is a program of broad-based study in the civilizations of Greece and Rome, with an emphasis on the literature and culture of the ancient world. Students take courses in Greek and Roman literature and culture, and they may choose to study ancient Greek or Latin as part of their major requirements. The major is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the history, literature, and culture of the ancient Mediterranean world. Students completing the Classical Civilization major should be able to: demonstrate broad-based knowledge of ancient Greek and Roman literature and culture; describe the history, literature, and culture of the ancient Mediterranean world; demonstrate knowledge of at least one ancient language (Greek or Latin), or demonstrate more in-depth knowledge of ancient culture through additional coursework in translation; and apply critical thinking and analytical skills to the study of the ancient world.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://catalog.registrar.ucla.edu/browse/Departments/Classics

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Climate Science
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Bachelor of Science in Climate Science, applicants must fulfill the general University of California admission requirements. This includes completing the required 'A-G' subject courses with a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) and submitting the UC application. The application requires students to answer Personal Insight Questions. While the major is housed in the Department of Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences, freshman applicants apply to the College of Letters and Science as 'Climate Science' or 'Pre-Climate Science' majors.
Description: The Climate Science major is designed to provide students with the scientific skills to understand and better predict the impacts of climate change and to develop solutions to mitigate its effects. Students will gain a deep understanding of the physical and chemical processes that govern the climate system, including the atmosphere, the oceans, and the cryosphere. The major also emphasizes the human dimensions of climate change, including the impacts on society, the environment, and the economy.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Cognitive Science
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Bachelor of Science in Cognitive Science, applicants must apply through the general University of California application. Admission is based on a comprehensive review of the applicant's academic history, including completion of the 'A-G' subject requirements with a minimum GPA. Applicants must submit the Personal Insight Questions. Students are typically admitted into the 'Pre-Cognitive Science' major and must complete specific preparatory courses—including psychology, calculus, and computer programming—with a minimum grade requirement to transition to the full major.
Concentration: Specialization in Computing
Description: Cognitive Science is the study of the mind. It is an interdisciplinary field that combines theories and methods from psychology, computer science, linguistics, philosophy, and neuroscience. The Cognitive Science major is designed to provide students with a thorough grounding in the study of the mind. The program offers a broad approach to the study of the mind, with emphasis on the integration of these disciplines. Students will learn about the nature of human intelligence, the development of the mind, and the relationship between the mind and the brain.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).

Requirements: Admission to the Communication major is highly competitive. Freshman applicants apply to the 'Pre-Communication' major via the University of California application. Admission is based on the general UCLA freshman review process, which includes academic achievement and Personal Insight Questions. Transfer applicants must apply directly to the Communication major and must have completed specific preparatory courses (including Communication 10 and three other courses from a list of related social sciences and humanities) with a minimum grade of C in each. A high GPA (minimum 3.7) is typically required for transfer consideration. All applicants must complete the University of California application, including the mandatory Personal Insight Questions.
Description: The Communication major at UCLA is a multidisciplinary curriculum leading to a Bachelor of Arts degree. It provides a solid foundation in the study of human communication, with an emphasis on three areas of study: mass communication and media institutions, interpersonal communication, and communication and culture. The curriculum is designed to provide students with a broad-based education in communication while allowing them to explore specific areas of interest in more depth.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Comparative Literature
Requirements: Admission to the Comparative Literature major is based on the standard University of California undergraduate admission requirements. Freshman applicants must complete the A-G subject requirements with a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents). Transfer applicants must complete 60 semester (90 quarter) units of transferable college credit with a minimum GPA of 3.2, including specific major preparation courses. Proficiency in at least one language other than English is required for the major.
Department: UCLA College of Letters and Science
Description: The Comparative Literature major provides students with a solid foundation in literary analysis and critical theory while offering flexibility for them to tailor their course of study to their individual interests. The major is designed for students who want to study literature and culture across national, linguistic, and disciplinary boundaries. It allows students to explore the intersections of different literary traditions and to investigate the ways in which literature relates to other forms of human expression, such as film, music, philosophy, and social theory.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.ithaca.edu/academics/majors-minors/all-undergraduate-majors

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computational and Systems Biology
Requirements: First-year applicants to UCLA can apply directly to the Pre-CaSB major. To declare the pre-major, a student must have completed at least one of the 7 pre-major prep courses at UCLA and have a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher. For transfer students, please check out the Transfer Students page for more information.
Department: UCLA College of Letters and Science
Concentration: Fundamental Research & Evolution
Description: The Fundamental Research & Evolution (FRE) concentration is intended for students who wish to pursue a research career in an academic or industrial environment. This concentration focuses on basic biological research using quantitative and computational methods, and includes a heavy emphasis on evolutionary biology. It is appropriate for students interested in basic research in many areas of biology, including ecology and evolution, physiology, and cell and molecular biology.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://casb.ucla.edu/fre/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Computer Engineering program at UCLA, applicants must meet the University of California’s minimum admission requirements: completion of 15 year-long 'A-G' college-preparatory courses with a grade of C or better, and a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents). Applicants must also submit the UC application including the four Personal Insight Questions. The Samueli School of Engineering specifically evaluates applicants on their academic preparation, particularly in mathematics and science, and performance in these subjects is a primary factor in the selection process.
Department: Henry Samueli School of Engineering and Applied Science
Description: The computer engineering program is a joint program between the Computer Science Department and the Electrical and Computer Engineering Department. The program is designed to provide a strong background in both electrical engineering and computer science. It provides students with a solid foundation in both hardware and software, and the skills to design and implement complex systems that integrate both. The curriculum includes courses in computer hardware, software, and systems. Students learn about the design, analysis, and application of computer systems, from tiny microprocessors to large-scale data centers. The program emphasizes both theoretical foundations and practical hands-on experience.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).
Accredidation: The Computer Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the UCLA Samueli School of Engineering, freshman applicants must meet the University of California’s 'A-G' course requirements and have a minimum 3.0 GPA (3.4 for non-residents). Specifically for Computer Science, applicants are expected to have a strong background in mathematics and science, including completion of at least one year of high school chemistry and physics, and at least three years of high school mathematics, including calculus. Transfer applicants must complete lower-division requirements including calculus, physics, and computer science courses with a minimum competitive GPA.
Department: Henry Samueli School of Engineering and Applied Science
Description: The Computer Science curriculum is designed to accommodate students who want a professional education in computer science but who may also have interests in other areas. The Computer Science program is designed to provide a strong foundation in the principles of computer science, and to prepare students for professional practice in the computer field and for graduate study. The curriculum is a design-oriented program that provides students with a broad background in the field. It provides a solid foundation in the fundamental principles of mathematics, science, and computer science, and also gives students the opportunity to explore a variety of topics in computer science and other fields through its elective and technical breadth requirements.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).
Accredidation: The Computer Science program is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science and Engineering
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UCLA, you must complete 15 year-long high school courses (the A-G courses) with a grade of C or better — at least 11 of them prior to your last year of high school. You must earn a grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 or better (3.4 for non-residents) in these courses with no grade lower than a C. Applicants to the Samueli School of Engineering are also evaluated on their academic preparation in studies such as mathematics and physics.
Description: The computer science and engineering curriculum at UCLA provides students with the education and training necessary to design, implement, test, and utilize the hardware and software of digital computers and digital systems. The program has been designed to provide a background of computer science and computer engineering as well as a more general background in engineering and the physical sciences. It also includes the study of various elective areas such as computer systems, computer networks, computer graphics, artificial intelligence, and database systems.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).
Accredidation: The Computer Science and Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, and the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

Requirements: Applicants must complete the University of California Application for Undergraduate Admission by the November 30 deadline. In addition to the UC Application, applicants must also complete a WACD Supplemental Application. Applicants for the Dance major are selected by the Dance faculty based on their UC application, supplemental application, and an audition/interview.
Department: UCLA School of the Arts and Architecture
Description: The Dance major is a program that integrates the study of choreography, performance, and world arts and cultures. It provides a foundation for students who wish to pursue careers in professional dance, choreography, teaching, or further study in dance and related fields. Students engage in technical training, creative research, and critical analysis of dance in various cultural and historical contexts.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://wac.ucla.edu/media/pages/programs/undergraduate/1826802650-1726854778/2024-2025-wacd-undergraduate-handbook.pdf
Accredidation: Member of the National Association of Schools of Dance (NASD)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Data Theory
Requirements: The Data Theory major is a capstone major. Admission to the major is competitive. Freshman applicants should apply to UCLA as a Pre-Data Theory major and are reviewed by the UCLA Undergraduate Admission office. To be considered for the Data Theory major, transfer students must complete the following courses by the end of the spring term prior to transfer: one year of calculus, multivariable calculus, linear algebra, and one computer programming course (C++, Python, or Java).
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Data Theory is a joint program between the Department of Mathematics and the Department of Statistics. Data Theory is an intensive major that provides a foundation in the mathematical and statistical theory that underlies modern data science. It provides the skills needed for success in graduate school or in careers as a data scientist.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://datatheory.ucla.edu/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Design | Media Arts
Requirements: All applicants to Design Media Arts must submit the UC application. In addition, applicants must submit the Department of Design Media Arts (DMA) supplemental application. The supplemental application includes a questionnaire, a statement of interest, and a creative portfolio.
Department: School of the Arts and Architecture
Description: The undergraduate major in Design Media Arts (DMA) is a multidisciplinary program that emphasizes a balance between aesthetic, creative, and critical thinking with proficiency in state-of-the-art technology. It focuses on the use of computers and other digital media for artistic expression and communication. Students are encouraged to develop their own personal vision while gaining a strong foundation in media history, theory, and practice. The DMA curriculum is organized around four main areas: visual communication and image, video and animation, networking and interactivity, and game design. Students take core courses in these areas and then choose from a variety of electives to tailor their studies to their interests. The program prepares students for careers in the media arts and design industries or for graduate study.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.design.ucla.edu/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Earth and Environmental Science
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in Earth and Environmental Science, applicants must meet the general University of California admission requirements. This includes completion of the A–G high school course pattern and submission of the University of California application, which includes the Personal Insight Questions. Specific preparation for the major involves introductory courses in Earth, Planetary, and Space Sciences, Chemistry (14A and 14B, or 20A and 20B), and Mathematics or Life Sciences (Life Sciences 7A, 30A, Mathematics 3A, or 31A).
Description: The Earth and Environmental Science BA program is intended to provide a broad background in Earth sciences that is especially appropriate for students intending to become K through 12 teachers in Earth, physical, or life sciences. It may also be appropriate for students who plan to enter careers in environmental law, government or public policy, or business.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Ecology, Behavior, and Evolution
Requirements: To be admitted to the major, students must complete the following preparatory courses with a grade of C- or better in each and a combined grade-point average of 2.0 or higher: Life Sciences 7A, 7B, 7C, and 23L; Chemistry and Biochemistry 14A, 14B, 14BL, and 14C, or 20A, 20B, 20L, and 30A; Mathematics 3A, 3B, and 3C, or 31A, 31B, and 32A, or Life Sciences 30A and 30B; Physics 5A, 5B, and 5C, or 1A, 1B, 1C, 4AL, and 4BL. Freshman applicants must also meet general University of California admission requirements, including the A-G subject sequence.
Description: The Ecology, Behavior, and Evolution major is designed for students wishing to specialize in these areas. It is appropriate for students intending to pursue graduate studies in these fields or for students interested in careers in areas such as environmental biology, animal behavior, conservation, or teaching.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).

Requirements: To enter the Economics major, students must first be a Pre-Economics major. Students must apply for the Economics major after they have completed the following pre-major courses with a 2.5 grade-point average and a 'C' or better in each course: Economics 1, 2, 11, 41; Writing II; and Mathematics 31A, 31B. For transfer students, the following courses are required for admission: one course in microeconomics, one course in macroeconomics, and two courses in calculus. All pre-major and major courses must be taken for a letter grade.
Concentration: Specialization in Computing
Description: The UCLA Economics Department is among the best in the world. Our distinguished faculty provide a top-notch education through three undergraduate majors: Economics, Business Economics, and Mathematics/Economics. Our curriculum is designed to teach students the skills they will need to succeed in their future careers and in life. Whether a student is interested in finance, public policy, or academia, UCLA Economics has something for everyone. In all three majors, students receive a rigorous foundation in economic theory and its applications. Each major also offers students the opportunity to choose from a wide range of elective courses that allow them to explore their interests in more depth. The economics major is the most flexible of the three majors. It is designed for students who want to study economics from a broad perspective. Students in the economics major have the opportunity to take courses in a variety of areas, including microeconomics, macroeconomics, econometrics, and more.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://economics.ucla.edu/undergraduate/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Education and Social Transformation
Requirements: Required: Education 10 or 11 (must be completed with a grade of B or better); One course from: Anthropology 3, Communication 1, Geography 3, Geography 6, Political Science 40, Psychology 10, or Sociology 1; One introductory course in statistics from: Statistics 10, 12, or 13.
Department: School of Education and Information Studies
Description: The Education and Social Transformation major is for students who want to use the tools of scholarly inquiry to better understand and solve the most pressing issues in education today. This major is for students who are interested in exploring how education can be used as a tool for social change and justice. The major provides students with a solid foundation in the study of education, including the historical, social, and political contexts of schooling. Students will learn to analyze educational policies and practices, and to develop innovative solutions to educational challenges.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://admission.ucla.edu/apply/transfer/deciding-on-major/major-preparation-education

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering
Requirements: Admission to the UCLA Samueli School of Engineering is highly selective and based on a comprehensive review of the UC Application. Requirements include completion of the 'A-G' subject requirements, a strong GPA (minimum 3.0 for California residents and 3.4 for non-residents), and the Personal Insight Questions. For engineering applicants, there is a specific emphasis on achievement in mathematics and science courses.
Department: Henry Samueli School of Engineering and Applied Science
Concentration: Circuits and Embedded Systems; Physical and Wave Electronics; Signals and Systems
Description: The Electrical Engineering curriculum provides a balanced education in the fundamentals of engineering, mathematics, and science, as well as a solid foundation in the core areas of electrical engineering. The curriculum is also designed to provide students with a broad education in the humanities and social sciences, as well as an appreciation for the social, economic, and ethical context of their professional work. The electrical engineering program is designed to prepare students for a professional career in industry, government, or academia.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).

Requirements: To be considered for admission to the English major, freshman applicants must complete the University of California (UC) application, which includes the secondary school 'a-g' requirements with a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents). Applicants must also respond to four Personal Insight Questions. For the major specifically, students enter as Pre-English and must complete English 10A, 10B, and 10C with a grade of C or better to satisfy the requirements for the major.
Concentration: Creative Writing Concentration, Specialization in Computing
Description: The English major at UCLA provides students with a comprehensive foundation in the history of literature in English and the tools of critical and creative analysis. Our students learn to read closely, think critically, and write clearly and persuasively. They engage with a diverse range of texts and cultures, from the medieval period to the present day, and they develop the skills they need to succeed in a wide range of careers.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://english.ucla.edu/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Science
Requirements: To declare the Environmental Science major, students must have completed all of the following: Environment 10; Statistics (Life Sciences 40, Stats 10, or Stats 13); Chemistry 14A/20A and 14B/20B; Mathematics 3A/31A and 3B/31B. In addition, students must have a minimum 2.0 (C) grade-point average in all prep courses for the major.
Department: Institute of the Environment and Sustainability
Concentration: Applied Ecology, Climate Science, Environmental Health, Environmental Systems and Society, GIS and Technologies, Marine Biology, and Restoration Ecology
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Environmental Science is an interdisciplinary program that allows students to study the environment from a variety of perspectives. The major provides a firm foundation in the natural sciences and includes a core of social sciences and humanities courses. Each student also completes a year-long senior practicum, working in a team on a real-world environmental project for a client.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.ioes.ucla.edu/envisci/how-to-declare-the-major/

Requirements: Applicants must first complete the University of California Undergraduate Application between October 1 and November 30. Additionally, all applicants to the Herb Alpert School of Music must submit a supplemental application. For the Ethnomusicology BA, the supplemental application requirements include a 1-2 page personal statement, a 1-2 page resume, two letters of recommendation, unofficial transcripts, and a video audition or portfolio submission. Applicants who pass the initial screening will be invited to an on-campus or virtual interview/audition.
Concentration: World Music
Description: The Ethnomusicology BA provides students with a broad-based education in ethnomusicology, focusing on the study of music as a social and cultural phenomenon. Students develop skills in musical performance and analysis while engaging with diverse musical traditions from around the globe. This concentration prepares students for a variety of careers in music, as well as for further study in ethnomusicology, musicology, and other related fields.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in European Languages and Transcultural Studies
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in European Languages and Transcultural Studies, applicants must complete the University of California application. General requirements include the completion of 15 year-long high school courses (A-G requirements) with a minimum GPA, and responses to four Personal Insight Questions. UCLA uses a holistic review process that considers academic achievements as well as personal qualities and contributions to the campus. UCLA is test-free and does not consider SAT or ACT scores for admission or scholarship purposes.
Concentration: French and Francophone Studies, German Studies, Italian Studies, Scandinavian Studies, European Studies
Description: The Department of European Languages and Transcultural Studies (ELTS) offers a Bachelor of Arts degree in European Languages and Transcultural Studies with five concentrations: (1) French and Francophone Studies, (2) German Studies, (3) Italian Studies, (4) Scandinavian Studies, and (5) European Studies. The major is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the languages, literatures, and cultures of Europe and the broader world shaped by European influence. The major offers students the opportunity to develop high-level proficiency in a European language while engaging with a diverse range of transcultural themes, including migration, colonialism, gender and sexuality, media, and environmental humanities. By exploring the complex histories and contemporary realities of European and transcultural contexts, students develop critical thinking, analytical, and communication skills that prepare them for a variety of careers in a globalized world.
ProgramWebsiteURL: http://us.51liucheng.com/niversity-of-california,-los-angeles-477/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in European Languages and Transcultural Studies with French and Francophone
Requirements: To apply for admission to UCLA, students must complete the University of California (UC) Application. Freshman applicants must satisfy the A-G subject requirements with a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) and complete the Personal Insight Questions. For transfer applicants, UCLA requires a strong GPA in major-specific preparatory coursework. The Department of European Languages and Transcultural Studies does not require a supplemental application or portfolio for this major.
Concentration: French and Francophone
Description: The major in European Languages and Transcultural Studies provides students with a foundation in one or more European languages and cultures. It is designed to provide students with a broad and deep understanding of the historical and cultural developments of Europe and its global impact. Through an interdisciplinary approach, students engage with literature, film, philosophy, and history to explore the complexities of European identities and their interactions with the rest of the world. Students select one of four sections: French and Francophone, German, Italian, or Scandinavian. The French and Francophone track provides students with a foundation in the French language and the diverse cultures and literatures of the French-speaking world, including France, Africa, the Caribbean, and North America.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in European Languages and Transcultural Studies with German
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UCLA, applicants must complete the University of California's 'a-g' subject requirements with a grade of C or better. Concentration: German
Description: The Department of European Languages and Transcultural Studies offers a major in European Languages and Transcultural Studies with five different concentrations: French and Francophone Studies, German, Italian, Scandinavian, and Transcultural Studies. The department's curriculum is designed to provide students with a deep understanding of the historical, social, and cultural contexts that have shaped European identities. Our programs are designed to help students develop high-level proficiency in a European language, as well as the critical thinking and analytical skills needed to succeed in a globalized world.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://admission.ucla.edu/apply/majors

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in European Languages and Transcultural Studies with Italian
Requirements: ELTS 1, Italian 1-6 or equivalent.

Description: European Languages and Transcultural Studies (ELTS) is the result of a merger between the departments of French & Francophone Studies, Germanic Languages, Italian, and Scandinavian. ELTS students explore European cultures through an experimental, transdisciplinary lens. While focusing on a specific language (French, German, Italian, or Scandinavian), students are encouraged to seek out connections between their primary area of study and the rest of Europe and beyond. The curriculum for each concentration is designed around four pillars of study: Experimental Humanities, Medical Humanities, Environmental Humanities, and Urban Humanities.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://reslife.ucla.edu/major-blast/humanities

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in European Languages and Transcultural Studies with Scandinavian
Requirements: To be eligible for admission as a freshman, applicants must complete 15 year-long college-preparatory courses (A-G requirements) with a grade of C or better: 2 years of History, 4 years of English, 3 years of Mathematics, 2 years of Science, 2 years of Language other than English, 1 year of Visual and Performing Arts, and 1 year of College-preparatory Elective. Applicants must earn a grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 or better (3.4 for non-California residents) in these courses. Admission also requires completion of the University of California application, which includes the Personal Insight Questions.
Concentration: Scandinavian
Description: The Department of European Languages and Transcultural Studies (ELTS) brings together UCLA’s distinguished programs in French, Germanic, Italian, and Scandinavian languages, literatures, and cultures. This union allows for a reimagining of our fields within a shared transcultural framework that addresses the complex history and the current state of Europe and its diverse global impact. The ELTS curriculum explores the intersections of language, literature, culture, and society, with an emphasis on interdisciplinary and transcultural perspectives. Students engage with a wide range of texts and media, from medieval manuscripts to contemporary film, and develop critical thinking, analytical, and communication skills. The European Languages and Transcultural Studies major is a single major with four tracks: French and Francophone Studies, German Studies, Italian Studies, and Scandinavian. Students must select one of the tracks.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in European Studies
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in European Studies, applicants must complete the University of California (UC) application. General requirements for admission to UCLA include completion of the 'A-G' secondary school course requirements, a minimum GPA of 3.0 for California residents (3.4 for non-residents), and completion of the Personal Insight Questions. The European Studies major requires students to complete specific lower-division preparation courses, including foreign language proficiency through the intermediate level (six quarters or equivalent).
Concentration: Humanities, Social Thought, or Europe in the World
Description: The European Studies major is an interdisciplinary program that allows students to study Europe from a variety of perspectives. Students choose a concentration in one of three areas: (1) Social Thought, (2) Humanities, or (3) Europe in the World. Within each concentration, students are encouraged to pursue their own interests by choosing from a wide range of courses in different departments.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Film and Television
Requirements: To apply for the Film and Television BA program, applicants must complete the University of California Undergraduate Application and the UCLA School of Theater, Film and Television Supplemental Application. Required supplemental materials include a Personal Statement (no more than 2 pages, double-spaced), Writing Samples (a one-page Creative Writing sample and a Critical Essay of no more than 3 pages), and a list of Life Experience/Special Achievement. Freshman applicants must also complete the Personal Insight Questions on the UC Application.
Department: UCLA School of Theater, Film and Television
Concentration: film production (directing or cinematography), screenwriting, animation or digital media
Description: The Department of Film, Television and Digital Media (FTVDM) is one of the most prestigious programs in the world. Our mission is to educate the next generation of storytellers, scholars and leaders in the field. Undergraduate students take a variety of courses that provide them with a well-rounded education in the history, theory and practice of film, television and digital media. In their first two years, students focus on general education and lower-division requirements. In their junior and senior years, they dive into the major, taking courses in film history, theory and production. Seniors concentrate on an area of specialization such as film production (directing or cinematography), screenwriting, animation or digital media.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.tft.ucla.edu/admissions/film-television-and-digital-media/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Gender Studies
Requirements: To enter the Gender Studies major, students must have an overall grade-point average of 2.0 or better and have completed Gender Studies 10 with a grade of C or better. Preparation for the major includes Gender Studies 10 and one course from Gender Studies 102 through 187. All applicants must complete the University of California (UC) application, which includes Personal Insight Questions and a review of academic history.
Department: UCLA College of Letters and Science
Description: The Gender Studies major is an interdisciplinary program that examines the construction of gender and its intersection with other social categories such as race, class, ethnicity, and sexuality. Students explore how gendered experiences are shaped by history, culture, and power structures. The program is designed to give students a multi-disciplinary and rigorous understanding of the ways that gender and other categories of identity shape our world. Students will learn how to analyze and critique the structures of power that produce inequality and to imagine and work towards more just and equitable societies. The Department of Gender Studies at UCLA is a premier site for the study of women, gender, and sexuality, offering a broad, interdisciplinary program that explores the social and cultural construction of gender and the relationship between gender and other systems of power and difference.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).
