For freshman applicants, this includes the completion of 15 year-long academic courses (A-G courses) with a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) and the submission of Personal Insight Questions. For the Linguistics and Psychology major, specific preparation for the major includes: Linguistics 20, Psychology 10, Psychology 100A, Psychology 100B, and one course selected from Philosophy 7, 21, or 31. Transfer applicants should have completed 60 semester (90 quarter) units of transferable college credit with a focus on major preparation courses.
Description: The Linguistics and Psychology major is an interdisciplinary major that combines the study of the structure of language with the study of the mind. It is intended for students who are interested in the ways in which language is represented and processed in the human mind and how it is acquired by children.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Linguistics and Spanish
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Bachelor of Arts in Linguistics and Spanish, applicants must meet the general University of California undergraduate admission requirements. This includes completing a minimum of 15 year-long 'A-G' high school courses with at least a 3.0 GPA (3.4 for non-California residents). Applicants must submit the University of California application, which includes the Personal Insight Questions. The College of Letters and Science does not require or consider supplemental materials such as resumes or portfolios for this major. UCLA is a test-free institution and does not consider SAT or ACT scores for admission decisions.
Description: The Linguistics and Spanish major is designed for students with a strong interest in the Spanish language. It provides students with a solid foundation in both the theoretical study of language (linguistics) and the study of the Spanish language, including its history, structure, and literature.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Marine Biology
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Science in Marine Biology, freshman applicants must meet the University of California’s admission requirements, which include completing 15 year-long 'a-g' courses with a grade of C or better and a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents). Specifically for the Marine Biology major within the Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology, students must complete preparatory coursework in Life Sciences (7A, 7B, 7C, and 23L), Chemistry (14A, 14B, 14BL, 14C or 20A, 20B, 20L, 30A), Mathematics (LS 30A, 30B and Stats 13 or Math 3A, 3B, 3C), and Physics (5A, 5B, 5C). Transfer applicants must complete major-specific preparatory courses by the end of the spring term prior to transfer.
Department: Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology (within the UCLA College of Letters and Science)
Description: The Marine Biology major is designed for students who wish to specialize in the biology of marine organisms and their ecosystems. It provides students with a broad background in biology and allows for specialization in specific areas of marine biology through elective coursework.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).
ScholarshipAmount: Varies (e.g., Regents Scholarship: $2,000 annually; Alumni Scholarships: $6,000–$20,000 over four years)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Materials Engineering
Requirements: UCLA Samueli selection is based on a competitive review of the applicant’s entire UC application. At a minimum, all applicants must have completed the UC 'a-g' course requirements by the end of their senior year of high school. In addition, all applicants to the UCLA Samueli School of Engineering are expected to have a strong background in mathematics and sciences. Freshmen are expected to have completed at least four years of mathematics (through calculus) and at least three years of science (including one year of physics and one year of chemistry).
Description: The Materials Engineering major is a structured program that provides a broad base in the sciences and engineering, with a focus on the properties, processing, and application of materials. The program is designed to provide a broad-based foundation in the science and engineering of materials. It is intended to prepare students for a variety of careers in industry or for further study in graduate school. The program emphasizes the relationships between the structure, processing, properties, and performance of all classes of materials, including metals, ceramics, polymers, and electronic materials.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).
Accredidation: The Materials Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria and the Program Criteria for Materials, Metallurgical, Ceramics and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

Requirements: Admission to the major is limited. Students must apply for the major after completing the following preparation for the major courses—Mathematics 31A, 31B, 32A, 32B, 33A, 33B, Program in Computing 10A, and Economics 1, 2, 11—with a minimum grade-point average of 2.5 and a grade of C or better in each course. Transfer students must complete one year of calculus, one course in multivariable calculus, one course in linear algebra, one course in differential equations, and one year of microeconomics and macroeconomics with a minimum grade of C in each course (2.5 grade-point average) before transferring to UCLA.
Description: The Financial Actuarial Mathematics major is designed for students interested in working in the actuarial profession or in a field of quantitative finance. It provides students with a strong mathematical foundation and introductory knowledge in the areas of finance, economics, and computing. This major is also intended to help students prepare for the first three or four actuarial exams.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://catalog.registrar.ucla.edu/major/2025/FinancialActuarialMathematicsBS

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematics, Applied
Requirements: To be considered for admission to UCLA, applicants must meet the general University of California admission requirements. For freshman, this includes the completion of 15 year-long 'A-G' courses with a grade of C or better, with at least 11 finished prior to the start of the 12th grade. For transfer students to the Applied Mathematics major, completion of the following major preparation courses is required: Calculus I and II, Multivariable Calculus, Differential Equations, Linear Algebra, and one computer programming course (C++ preferred). Applicants must also complete the Personal Insight Questions as part of the University of California application.
Description: The Applied Mathematics major is intended for students who are interested in using mathematics to solve problems in the social and physical sciences. While the program’s core is composed of the standard courses in differential equations, modeling, and numerical analysis, it also allows students to select courses in areas such as engineering, physics, and economics.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematics/Applied Science
Requirements: Preparation for the Major: Mathematics 31A, 31B, 32A, 32B, 33A, 33B; Program in Computing 10A; and one of the following sequences: Chemistry and Biochemistry 20A, 20B; Economics 1, 2, 11; Physics 1A, 1B (or 1AH), 1C (or 1CH). All preparatory courses must be completed with a minimum overall 2.0 grade-point average. To enter the Mathematics/Applied Science major, students must have completed the first four courses with a 2.5 grade-point average or better at UCLA and a minimum grade of C in each course. Transfer students must complete Math 31A, 31B, 32A, 32B, 33A, and 33B by the end of the spring term prior to transfer.
Concentration: Applied Mathematics, Medical and Life Sciences, and History of Science
Description: The Mathematics/Applied Science major is designed for students who are interested in applications of mathematics to other areas. This major is not intended for students who are planning to do graduate work in mathematics. For those students, the Mathematics or Applied Mathematics major is more appropriate. This major offers 3 options: (1) Applied Mathematics, (2) Medical and Life Sciences, (3) History of Science.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://ww3.math.ucla.edu/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/2024-2025-Undergraduate-Handbook-Department-of-Mathematics-for-Print.pdf

Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Bachelor of Science in Mathematics/Economics program at UCLA, freshman applicants must complete the University of California (UC) application, including the Personal Insight Questions. Applicants must have completed a minimum of 15 year-long 'a-g' high school courses with at least 11 finished prior to their senior year, and they must have a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-California residents). UCLA uses a holistic review process that considers academic achievements, personal qualities, and life experiences. Transfer applicants must complete specific major preparation courses, including calculus, linear algebra, and micro/macroeconomics, prior to admission.
Description: The Mathematics/Economics major is designed to give students a solid foundation in both mathematics and economics, stressing those areas of mathematics that are most relevant to economics and the parts of economics that emphasize the use of mathematics. It is a rigorous program that provides students with the mathematical tools necessary for graduate study in economics and for careers in finance and other quantitative fields.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematics for Teaching
Requirements: Preparation for the major: Mathematics 31A, 31B, 32A, 32B, 33A, 33B; Program in Computing 10A; Physics 1A (or 1AH) or 5A or 6A. Each course must be completed with a C- or better and an overall combined 2.0 GPA. All courses must be taken for a letter grade. Students must also complete the major requirements which include Math 115A, 131A, 105A, 105B, 105C, 117, 123, 161, and Statistics 100A.
Description: The Mathematics for Teaching major is designed for students who have a substantial interest in teaching mathematics at the secondary school level. This major provides students with a solid foundation in mathematics, including geometry, algebra, and analysis, as well as exposure to the pedagogical aspects of the subject. Students have the opportunity to participate in the Joint Mathematics/Education Program (JMEP), which allows them to complete their degree and begin work toward a California Single Subject Teaching Credential in mathematics while still an undergraduate.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://ww3.math.ucla.edu/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/2023-2024-Undergraduate-Handbook-Department-of-Mathematics.pdf

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematics of Computation
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Science in Mathematics of Computation at UCLA, applicants must submit the University of California application and answer four Personal Insight Questions. Freshman applicants must complete 15 'a-g' high school courses with a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents). Specific preparation for the major includes completing a series of courses: Mathematics 31A, 31B, 32A, 32B, 33A, 33B; Physics 1A, 1B, 1C and 4AL/4BL (or Physics 5A, 5B, 5C); and Program in Computing 10A, 10B, and 10C. Admission to the major is contingent upon grades in these preparatory courses. UCLA is test-free and does not consider SAT or ACT scores for admission or scholarship purposes.
Description: The Mathematics of Computation major is designed for students who are interested in the application of mathematics to computer science and the use of computers in solving mathematical problems. It provides students with a solid foundation in mathematics and a substantial background in computer science.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://degrees.unm.edu/units/7430/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering program at UCLA, freshman applicants must complete the University of California (UC) Application and meet the following criteria: completion of the 'A-G' subject requirements (History, English, Mathematics, Science, Language other than English, Visual and performing arts, and College-preparatory elective) with a minimum GPA; and submission of the Personal Insight Questions. For the Samueli School of Engineering, admission is highly selective and based on academic preparation, particularly in mathematics and science. Transfer applicants must complete specific lower-division preparation courses including calculus, physics, and chemistry before transferring.
Description: The mechanical engineering program is designed to provide basic knowledge in thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, solid mechanics, mechanical design, and control systems, as well as to develop skills in using analytical, computational, and experimental methods for the solution of engineering problems. The program objectives for the mechanical engineering major are (1) to provide graduates with a solid foundation in engineering and basic sciences that will enable them to succeed in graduate school or in their careers in industry or government, (2) to provide graduates with the ability to design and build mechanical systems, and (3) to provide graduates with a broad education that will allow them to appreciate the impact of engineering solutions in a global and societal context.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).
Accredidation: The mechanical engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Microbiology, Immunology, and Molecular Genetics
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UCLA as a freshman, you must meet the following requirements: 1. Complete 15 year-long high school courses with a grade of C or better — at least 11 of them prior to your last year of high school (A-G requirements). 2. Earn a grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 or better (3.4 if you're a nonresident of California) in these courses with no grade lower than a C. Students are admitted to the Microbiology, Immunology, and Molecular Genetics major as 'Pre-Microbiology, Immunology, and Molecular Genetics' majors. Admission to the major is subject to completion of specific preparatory courses including Chemistry, Life Sciences, Mathematics, and Physics.
Department: College of Letters and Science (Division of Life Sciences)
Description: The Microbiology, Immunology, and Molecular Genetics major provides a broad educational background in microbiology, immunology, and molecular genetics. The program is designed to prepare students for graduate study in these and related fields, for admission to health professional schools, or for employment in the biotechnology industry, government, and academia.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).
ScholarshipType: Merit-based (Regents), Need-based (Blue and Gold Opportunity Plan)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Middle Eastern Studies
Requirements: The major in Middle Eastern Studies is a multidisciplinary program designed to provide students with a broad background in the languages, history, and cultures of the Middle East. To enter the major, students must have an overall grade-point average of 2.0 or better. For transfer students, required preparation includes one year of a Middle Eastern language (e.g., Arabic, Armenian, Hebrew, Persian, or Turkish), and one civilization course is recommended. General admission requires the UC application and responses to Personal Insight Questions. UCLA is test-free and does not consider SAT or ACT scores for admission or scholarship purposes.
Description: Middle Eastern Studies is a multi-disciplinary major designed for students who wish to study the region from a variety of perspectives, including history, politics and culture. This major is often pursued as a double major with other fields such as Political Science, History, or Anthropology. Middle Eastern Studies majors are required to take courses in at least two of the following areas: Anthropology, Art History, Economics, Ethnomusicology, Geography, History, Political Science, and Sociology.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://nelc.ucla.edu/undergraduate/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Molecular, Cell, and Developmental Biology
Requirements: To be admitted to the Molecular, Cell, and Developmental Biology major, students must complete the following preparation for the major courses with a grade of C or better in each course and an overall grade-point average of 2.0 or better: Life Sciences 7A, 7B, 7C, 23L; Chemistry and Biochemistry 14A, 14B, 14BL, 14C, and 14D, or 20A, 20B, 20L, 30A, 30AL, and 30B; Mathematics 3A, 3B, and 3C, or 31A, 31B, and 32A, or Life Sciences 30A and 30B; Physics 5A, 5B, and 5C, or 1A, 1B, 1C, 4AL, and 4BL.
Department: UCLA College (Letters and Science), Division of Life Sciences
Description: Molecular, Cell and Developmental Biology is a multifaceted discipline that examines how organisms function, from the level of individual molecules to the complex interactions within and between cells. It explores the mechanisms governing gene expression, cellular organization, and the intricate processes of development. Understanding these fundamental aspects is essential for addressing key challenges in medicine, agriculture, and environmental science. Research in this field is constantly evolving, driven by technological advancements that allow us to delve deeper into the mysteries of life. From studying the structure of proteins to unraveling the complexities of human development, Molecular, Cell and Developmental Biology offers a vast and fascinating landscape for exploration and discovery.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.mcdb.ucla.edu/undergraduate/

Requirements: Applicants for the Bachelor of Music in Composition must complete the University of California Undergraduate Application and a UCLA Herb Alpert School of Music supplemental application. Specific requirements for the supplemental application include a portfolio of three to four original scores along with recordings (live recordings are preferred, but MIDI is acceptable), a musical experience outline (resume), and a personal statement.
Department: The UCLA Herb Alpert School of Music
Description: The composition program at UCLA provides a select group of students the opportunity to develop their creative voices through intensive study with a distinguished faculty. The curriculum is designed to provide a strong foundation in the craft of composition, including orchestration, counterpoint, and electronic music, while encouraging students to explore diverse aesthetic directions and interdisciplinary collaborations. The major includes courses in music theory, music history, performance, and individual composition lessons.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).
Accredidation: The Herb Alpert School of Music at UCLA is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Music Education
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Music Education major, applicants must complete the University of California Application and the UCLA Herb Alpert School of Music Supplemental Application. The supplemental application requires a personal statement, two letters of recommendation, one music teacher recommendation, a repertoire list or resume, and unofficial transcripts. Additionally, applicants must participate in an audition and interview as part of the selection process.
Department: The Herb Alpert School of Music
Description: The Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) in Music Education is a professional degree that provides students with the musical knowledge, pedagogical skills, and teaching experience necessary for a career in music education. The Music Education major prepares students for careers as music teachers in public and private schools (K-12). It provides the broad background in music theory, history, and performance required for all music majors, and adds a comprehensive program of study in music education. Students in the program develop the skills, knowledge, and perspectives necessary for effective teaching in a variety of musical settings. They complete coursework in the philosophy and history of music education, child and adolescent development, instructional technology, and teaching methods for diverse learners. In addition, students gain practical experience through supervised field observations and student teaching in local schools. Graduates of the program are eligible to apply for the California Preliminary Single Subject Teaching Credential in Music, which is required for teaching music in California public schools.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://schoolofmusic.ucla.edu/academics/music/music-education-ba/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Music History and Industry
Requirements: Applicants must complete the University of California Undergraduate Application and a program-specific supplemental application for the Herb Alpert School of Music. Supplemental requirements for the Music History and Industry BA include: unofficial transcripts, a personal statement (maximum 500 words) explaining interest in the major and career goals, one writing sample (preferably an essay on a music-related topic), a music resume (maximum two pages) summarizing music-related training and experience, and one letter of recommendation. Applicants may also submit an optional portfolio of creative work. UCLA does not consider SAT or ACT scores for undergraduate admission.
Description: The Music History and Industry major provides a unique curriculum that combines a traditional musicology foundation with music industry coursework and professional development. It is intended for students who want to study music as a global phenomenon, explore music’s roles in past and present societies, and develop an understanding of the contemporary music industry. Students complete a sequence of core courses in musicology and music industry, along with elective courses that allow them to focus on areas such as film music, popular music, global music, music business, and music technology. All students complete a music industry internship as part of the degree. The BA degree in Music History and Industry is an ideal choice for students who want to pursue a wide variety of careers in the music industry or go on to graduate study in musicology or related fields.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).
Accredidation: The UCLA Herb Alpert School of Music is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Music in Music Performance
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Music in Music Performance at UCLA, applicants must complete both the University of California Application and the Herb Alpert School of Music Supplemental Application. Specific requirements include a music resume (detailing musical background and experience), a 500-word personal statement, letters of recommendation, and a successful audition or pre-screening recording. Applicants must also meet the general University of California admission requirements, including the completion of the 'A-G' subject requirements.
Description: The Bachelor of Music in Music Performance program is designed for students who wish to pursue a career as a professional musician. This professional degree offers students the opportunity to specialize in one of several areas of study, including strings, woodwinds, brass, percussion, piano, and voice. Students receive private instruction from our world-renowned faculty and participate in a wide variety of ensembles, from large orchestras to small chamber groups. The curriculum is designed to provide students with a high level of technical training and musical knowledge, preparing them for careers as professional performers, teachers, and scholars.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://music.apple.com/us/artist/bm/1457842098
Accredidation: The UCLA Herb Alpert School of Music is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

Requirements: All applicants for the Bachelor of Arts in Musicology must submit the University of California Undergraduate Application by November 30. In addition, applicants must complete the Herb Alpert School of Music Supplemental Application, which includes a personal statement, a resume, and a writing sample. There is no performance audition required for this major. UCLA is test-free and does not consider SAT or ACT scores for admission purposes.
Department: The Herb Alpert School of Music
Description: The Musicology major provides a foundation for students who want to study music and its historical, social, and cultural contexts. The curriculum covers a wide range of musical styles, including Western art music, jazz, popular music, and world music. Students develop critical thinking, writing, and research skills through courses in music history, theory, and analysis. The Musicology major is designed for students who want to explore music as a humanistic discipline and prepares them for a variety of careers in music, education, media, and the arts, as well as for graduate study in musicology or related fields.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).
Accredidation: The UCLA Herb Alpert School of Music is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

Requirements: To be eligible to declare the Neuroscience major, students must have completed all of the pre-major courses with a grade of C- or better in each course and a cumulative GPA of 2.0 or higher. Pre-major courses include: Life Sciences 7A, 7B, 7C, 23L; Chemistry and Biochemistry 14A, 14B, 14BL, 14C (or 20A, 20B, 20L, 30A); Mathematics 3A, 3B, 3C (or 31A, 31B, 32A or Life Sciences 30A, 30B); Physics 5A, 5B, 5C (or 1A, 1B, 1C, 4AL, 4BL). All courses must be taken for a letter grade.
Description: The Neuroscience major is a multi-disciplinary program that provides a broad background in the biological and physical sciences and a focused understanding of the nervous system. The curriculum includes a core of courses in biology, chemistry, and physics, followed by specialized courses in neuroanatomy, neurophysiology, and neurochemistry.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.neurosci.ucla.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2021/03/Updated-NS-Minor-Sheet-3.21.pdf

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Nordic Studies
Requirements: To be considered for admission to UCLA, applicants must meet the University of California’s minimum admission requirements. Freshman applicants must complete the A-G subject requirements with a grade of C or better and submit the UC Application, which includes the Personal Insight Questions. For the Nordic Studies major, which is housed in the College of Letters and Science, there are no supplemental application requirements beyond the general university application. Transfer students are expected to complete lower-division preparation for the major, which includes three courses from Scandinavian 1 through 50 or equivalent.
Description: The Nordic Studies Major provides students with the opportunity to explore the cultures and languages of the Nordic region, including Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, and Sweden. Students gain proficiency in one of the three mainland Scandinavian languages (Danish, Norwegian, or Swedish) and explore Nordic literature, film, history, and society from a variety of perspectives.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Nursing - Prelicensure
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Science in Nursing - Prelicensure program at UCLA, applicants must complete the University of California Undergraduate Application and a School of Nursing Supplemental Application. High school applicants should have a strong academic record in college-preparatory courses, particularly in science and mathematics. Transfer applicants must have completed 90-105 quarter units (60-70 semester units) of college credit by the time of enrollment, including specific prerequisite courses such as Human Anatomy, Human Physiology, Chemistry (Inorganic, Organic, and Biochemistry), and Microbiology. A minimum cumulative GPA of 3.5 is generally expected for competitive applicants. The application process includes the UC Personal Insight Questions and supplemental nursing essays.
Description: The UCLA School of Nursing has a prelicensure program leading to the Bachelor of Science degree. The BS program is designed to prepare students for a career in nursing. The curriculum is designed to provide a strong foundation in the biological and social sciences, as well as the humanities, and to provide the clinical skills and knowledge necessary for entry-level nursing practice. Graduates of the program are eligible to take the National Council Licensure Examination (NCLEX) for registered nurses.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).
Accredidation: The baccalaureate degree program in nursing at the University of California, Los Angeles School of Nursing is accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE) and approved by the California Board of Registered Nursing (BRN).

Requirements: To be admitted to the Philosophy major, students must complete the following preparation for the major: Philosophy 7 or 21, 22, 31, and one other course from 1 through 30. All preparation courses must be taken for a letter grade (minimum C grade in each course; overall grade-point average of 2.0). Freshman applicants must satisfy the University of California’s A-G subject requirements and have a competitive grade point average. Transfer applicants should complete the preparation for the major courses prior to admission.
Description: Philosophy is the critical examination of the most fundamental concepts and assumptions of every area of human experience. It is the study of the nature of reality, knowledge, and value. The department offers a broad curriculum that covers the history of philosophy as well as contemporary work in ethics, political philosophy, metaphysics, epistemology, philosophy of language, philosophy of mind, and logic. The Philosophy major is designed to provide students with an understanding of the history of philosophy and the basic problems of the field and to develop their skills in critical thinking, logical analysis, and clear and effective writing.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and Need-based (e.g., Regents Scholarship, UCLA Achievement Scholarship)

Description: The Physics major is designed to provide a solid foundation in the principles of physics and its applications. It is intended to prepare students for graduate study in physics or related fields, or for professional careers in industry, government, or education. The curriculum includes courses in classical mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum mechanics, thermodynamics, and statistical mechanics, as well as laboratory courses and electives in specialized areas.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Physiological Science
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Science in Physiological Science at UCLA is based on general university requirements. Applicants must complete the University of California Application. For freshman applicants, this includes the completion of 'A-G' subject requirements and the Personal Insight Questions. For transfer students, admission is competitive and requires the completion of major preparation courses, including: Life Sciences 7A, 7B, and 7C; Chemistry and Biochemistry 14A, 14B, 14C (or 20A, 20B, 30A); Mathematics 3A, 3B, 3C (or 31A, 31B, 32A); and Physics 5A, 5B, 5C.
Description: The Physiological Science major provides a broad background in biology and the physical sciences, while emphasizing the physiology of organisms and organelles. The curriculum is designed to prepare students for graduate studies in physiology or other biological sciences and for professional training in medicine, dentistry, physical therapy, and other health-oriented fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Political Science
Requirements: To be considered for admission to UCLA, applicants must submit the University of California Application. Freshman applicants must complete 15 year-long 'A-G' high school courses with a grade of C or better, including 11 completed by the end of the junior year. A minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-California residents) is required in these courses. Admission is based on a holistic review of academic and personal achievements. Transfer applicants for the Political Science major must complete specific major preparation requirements: five lower-division courses including Introduction to Political Theory, World Politics, Comparative Politics, American Politics, and Introduction to Political Analysis (or an approved statistics course). Transfers must have a minimum 3.2 GPA in these major prep courses.
Concentration: American Politics, Comparative Politics, International Relations, Political Theory, Methods and Models, Race, Ethnicity, and Politics
Description: Political science is the study of politics and power from domestic, international, and comparative perspectives. It entails understanding political ideas, ideologies, institutions, policies, processes, and behavior, as well as groups, classes, government, diplomacy, law, strategy, and war. A political science education provides students with valuable diagnostic and analytical tools.
